clue.text: Rancour in African country church

parts.note: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Bitterness within a congregation somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is lasting bitterness or ill will, a close synonym of spite and malevolence.

clue.text: Virtuoso left band — no piano turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means read from bottom to top, so reversed
no piano means the p is dropped

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a seam is a band or layer of rock or coal

explanation.surface: A star player quits the group after the keyboard is removed from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT loses P ('no piano') to give ORT; with SEAM, 'turning up' reverses ORTSEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master musician or performer of great skill.

clue.text: Failure more relaxed missing an Oscar

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: looser means less tight, more relaxed
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A flop who got calmer after not winning an Academy Award.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails, a washout.

clue.text: Pardon prisoner executed

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
executed in the sense of carried out, done

explanation.surface: A convict reprieved, or put to death: a grim pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests a hanging, but it means carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive a wrong.

clue.text: Dog born with attractive feature

parts.note: an asset is a useful or appealing quality

explanation.surface: A puppy that arrived in the world with a winning trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: After training Rosa and Leo can type

indicators.note: after training they are put through new drills, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once taught, Rosa and Leo are able to do keyboard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can type' reads as able to type; it means a kind of can.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised spray canister, one variety of tin.

clue.text: Oil source seen in Van Gogh's art?

definitions.meaning: the plant's seeds are pressed for cooking oil
Van Gogh painted a famous series of still lifes of this flower in a vase

explanation.surface: Looking for oil paint in a Van Gogh canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall yellow plant yields seed oil and is the subject of Van Gogh's celebrated paintings.

clue.text: Set out to stop honest administrator

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, sitting inside the other word

parts.note: true means honest or faithful

indicators.note: out as in disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to block an upright manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like a phrase meaning arrange, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal, making STE; 'to stop' means plugging the honest word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee manages property or funds on behalf of others.

clue.text: A Liberal by coastal area in recess

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician beside the seaside during a parliamentary break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a holiday from Parliament, but it is a nook.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back into a wall.

clue.text: It is what it is

parts.note: read literally, the word 'it' is a grammatical item of a certain class, the category the answer names

explanation.surface: A shrugging catchphrase of resignation about something that cannot be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase hides a grammar lesson: the word 'It' is a member of the class the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as I, you, he and it stand for people or things, which is the grammar category of the answer.

clue.text: Sound system bent trees round

indicators.note: something bent is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hi-fi set somehow warped the trees around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be the adjective healthy, but it pairs with 'system'. 'bent' makes STERE; 'round' is the letter shape, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a domestic audio player with two channels of output.

clue.text: Dead fish taken in to be cooked

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is enclosed by the letters around it
cooked as in falsified or worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A dead fish brought into the kitchen to be cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TO BE into OBTE, which then takes SOLE inside after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is no longer in use, as good as defunct.

clue.text: Substantial clubs on Greek island

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A sizeable golf bag on holiday in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete in the sense of solid and real, existing in material form rather than abstract.

clue.text: Vehicle black and dirty not an eyesore

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: not an means those two letters are removed

parts.note: unclean means dirty

explanation.surface: A filthy dark motor that is somehow not unsightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles famously called a planned National Gallery extension a 'monstrous carbuncle', hence eyesore.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbuncle is used of an ugly building, an architectural blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Relaxed look at wicket by opener

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
a key opens a lock

explanation.surface: A calm cricket scene: watching the stumps as the opening batter takes guard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is one of the first two batters; here it is a thing that opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-key means restrained and casual, without fuss or tension.

clue.text: Craving beer at last in the present time

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the longer piece

parts.note: this refers to the one here now, the present one

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word beer

explanation.surface: Wanting a beer, finally, right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a strong desire, used figuratively for any longing, not just for drink.

clue.text: At sea the rain warrants cover for head

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, rain makes a hat necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn over the hair to hold it in place.

clue.text: Excursion allowed for one child in three?

parts.note: a trip is an outing
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A school outing permitted for one pupil in three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one child in three' sounds like a ratio; it is one of three born together.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is any of three children from a single birth.

clue.text: Create case for trade after classes

indicators.note: after places the trade piece behind the classes piece

parts.note: genera are taxonomic classes, plural of genus

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Making a business argument after lessons are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classes' means biological groupings here, not lessons; 'case for' is the outside of trade, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or bring into being, the same as making something.

clue.text: The fat of the land do we hear?

indicators.note: a question about hearing signals the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: Greece is a land, a country of southern Europe

explanation.surface: A twist on 'the fat of the land', the best of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is animal fat, especially melted or rendered.

clue.text: Party enforcing six-pack ban? Impossible

parts.note: no as a sign means a ban, as in no smoking
a six-pack holds cans, so one can stands for it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A dry party where beer is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as 'no can' + 'do' is a party banning cans.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal meaning it cannot be done.

clue.text: Really small marrow finally included in stew?

indicators.note: included means placed within the other word

parts.note: titchy is British slang for tiny

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of marrow

explanation.surface: A tiny vegetable tail tossed into a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCHY is British slang for very small. 'in stew' reads as cookery; to be in a stew is to be anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being agitated, the same jittery state as nervous.

clue.text: Soldier retreats to Ur breaking nice statuette

indicators.note: breaking means splitting a word open and entering it

parts.note: fine means pleasant or nice

indicators.note: a soldier retreating goes backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, taken as written

explanation.surface: An army man falls back to the ancient city, smashing a pleasant little statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' gives IG, an American soldier backwards; Ur is the Sumerian city, kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small sculpted figure, a little statue.

clue.text: Competition caught up with Bond

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: A contest where someone catches up with James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a knockout match in a football cup tournament, a sporting contest.

clue.text: Wartime captive meeting monarch might

parts.note: POW stands for prisoner of war
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war meets the King or Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun, strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and might both mean strength or force.

clue.text: Lunch packed with punch?

parts.note: a packed lunch with a filling that hits hard: British slang for a punch in the mouth

explanation.surface: A packed lunch with a spicy kick.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for a punch in the face, pictured here as a sandwich whose filling is a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means a blow to the mouth, a fist delivered like a meal.

clue.text: Banknote left in tray emptied

indicators.note: in puts the departing word inside the emptied tray
emptied removes the contents, leaving only the outside letters of tray

parts.note: went is the past of go, meaning left

explanation.surface: A note abandoned in a tray that has been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as the direction but is the past of go; 'emptied' keeps only the shell of tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A twenty is a twenty-pound or twenty-dollar note, named for its value.

clue.text: Outlaw keeping old brother in line

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a railway line
bro is informal for brother

explanation.surface: A villain keeping his aged sibling under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Roy MacGregor was an 18th-century Scottish outlaw and folk hero.
